item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is narrowly preferable because its Upload retry path is tested end-to-end and its retry change avoids A’s dangerous global buffering of arbitrary streams. Neither patch is merge-ready because both violate several explicit contract requirements.","reasons":["B tests multipart filename, field, content, validation, request options, and a 429 retry through Upload; A’s retry test exercises Add instead of Upload.","B leaves non-seekable Raw.Do bodies streamed once, whereas A eagerly reads every body into memory and materially changes unrelated request semantics.","B adds focused multipart helper tests and returns distinct validation errors."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts AddFileOption rather than FilesOption.","It adds prohibited association fields and duplicate option machinery, calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, and uses a new NewFileWithFields helper rather than established NewFile.","makeBodyReplayable buffers every arbitrary request body globally. If io.ReadAll fails, it silently returns after partially consuming the body, allowing a truncated request to be sent instead of propagating the reader error; it can also break streaming behavior or cause unbounded memory use."] ,"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong signature, adds prohibited association options, bypasses FilesService.Add, and uses NewFileWithFields instead of NewFile.","ensureReplayableBody is unreliable for the reported *os.File case: the initial request owns and closes the file, after which GetBody attempts to Seek the same closed object. Its test deliberately uses a seeker that is not an io.ReadCloser, so it misses this failure.","There is no source-reader-error test, and the retry test does not assert the uploaded content bytes on every attempt. Documentation also makes unsupported claims about *os.File replay and adds unrelated Update commentary."]}
